decisions.evidence: R1 maker: spec lists exclusions including 'automatic metadata retrieval' and 'automatically retrieving page titles, descriptions, favicons'. R1 client: 'when I save a link, I really don't want to type in the title... the app goes and grabs the page's title, its description, and its little icon for me, and fills those in — and then I can tweak them... Please bring that in.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Reference REF-BM-02/03 require auto-collection of metadata (editable); maker explicitly excluded it, contradicting the reference. Client rejects the exclusion and supplies the conforming behaviour (fetch + editable) -> corrective/correct. Re-presented conformingly in R2 ('editable suggestions, graceful failure').

decisions.evidence: R1 maker exclusions: 'imports... automatic metadata retrieval'. R1 client: 'Getting my existing bookmarks in, and my collection back out... bring them in from a standard bookmarks file, and export mine the same way... I saw import/export listed as excluded — I'd want those.' R2 maker: 'Standard browser bookmark HTML import/export... Folder-to-tag conversion.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Import/export (REF-BM-30/31, Netscape HTML) explicitly excluded, contradicting reference. Client rejects exclusion and states the conforming round-trip behaviour -> corrective/correct.

decisions.evidence: R1 spec omitted read-later. R1 client: 'A read later idea... mark it as unread and be able to look at just my unread pile, then mark things read as I get through them.' R2 maker: 'Unread/read status, with new bookmarks defaulting to unread.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Read-later/unread (REF-BM-17/18/19) absent from presented scope; client requests the missing reference requirements -> corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 spec omitted archiving. R1 client: 'Tucking links away without deleting them... move it out of my main list into a separate archived area I can still go back to — different from deleting, which should be permanent.' R2 maker: 'Archiving and restoration, separate from permanent deletion.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Archive vs delete (REF-BM-26/27/28) absent from presented scope; client requests missing reference requirements, distinguishing reversible archive from permanent delete -> corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 spec had only 'Search, tags, filtering'. R1 client: 'Smarter searching. Beyond plain text matching, I'd expect to search by a tag directly, put a phrase in quotes for an exact match, and combine terms (this and that, or not that).' R2 maker: 'Exact phrases, tag: criteria, and AND/OR/NOT search.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Tag search, quoted-phrase exact match, and boolean operators (REF-BM-14/15/16) absent from presented plain-text search; client requests the missing reference requirements -> corrective/extend. (tag: vs #tag syntax treated as functionally equivalent.)

decisions.evidence: R1 spec omitted bulk actions. R1 client: 'Handling a lot at once. If I select several links, I'd like to do one action to all of them — like tagging them or archiving them together.' R2 maker: 'Bulk tagging, status changes, archiving, restoration, and deletion.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Bulk multi-select actions (REF-BM-20) absent from presented scope; client requests the missing reference requirement -> corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R2 client (note present but rendering unstated): 'I can write a personal note... will it show up nicely formatted if I use simple things like a bit of bold or a bulleted list?... If notes display readably, go ahead and approve.' R3 maker: 'Notes will display as formatted content—paragraphs, bold, italic, lists.' R3 client: 'thank you for confirming the notes will show up properly formatted.'
decisions.note: Specification gate via clarification. REF-BM-23 requires rendering the markdown note when viewing; presented note feature left rendering unstated. Client surfaces the expectation as a gating condition; maker aligns; client accepts. Clarification+disposition counted once as corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: R2 client: 'since I can now build fairly specific searches, it'd be handy someday to save a search I use a lot so I can jump back to it without retyping. That can wait — no need to add it now.' Reaffirmed R3 ('fine with saved searches being a later addition') and R5. Feature never added.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Saved search = bundle (REF-BM-29) absent. Client explicitly names the expected behaviour and its difference from the presentation but accepts the departure without requesting alignment -> accepted_divergence, catch_type none. Counted once.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'duplicate handling'. R1 client: 'The re-saving behavior you described is exactly right — if I try to save something I already saved, point me at the one I've got rather than making a duplicate.' R5 client verified live: 'it stopped me and pointed me right at the one I already had.'
decisions.note: In-scope decision conforming to REF-BM-06 (re-save converges to editing existing). Recorded conforming; not an opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Reference REF-BM-10: 'On tag entry, offer existing tags as autocomplete.' No maker presentation (R1-R5) mentions tag autocomplete, and the client only requests tag assignment/search, never autocomplete. R5 client accepts without raising it.
decisions.note: Prototype/spec across stages. Autocomplete on tag entry (REF-BM-10) silently omitted throughout; no corrective or explicit expression of the difference -> unexpressed_divergence, caught=false.

decisions.evidence: Reference REF-BM-24 (local HTML snapshot, PDF-download rule) and REF-BM-25 (Internet Archive snapshot). No snapshot capability appears in any maker presentation (R1-R5) nor is raised by the client at any point, including the R5 acceptance.
decisions.note: Extended reference features (snapshot preservation) silently absent across all stages; client never surfaces the difference -> unexpressed_divergence, caught=false.

decisions.evidence: Reference REF-BM-32: adjust display settings (default sort, displayed items, font size). Sorting exists (REF-BM-22) but no user display-settings feature appears in any maker presentation (R1-R5) and the client never requests one.
decisions.note: User settings / display preferences (REF-BM-32) silently omitted; no corrective or expressed difference -> unexpressed_divergence, caught=false.

decisions.evidence: Reference REF-BM-02 requires auto-collecting title, description, favicon AND preview image. R2 maker delivers 'title, description, and favicon retrieval'; R5 maker: 'automatic page metadata and icon retrieval' — preview image never mentioned. Client's request (R1) also scoped only to 'title, description, and its little icon'; preview image never raised.
decisions.note: Separable sub-requirement of REF-BM-02. The auto-fetch was corrected (see decision 1), but the preview-image portion diverges (omitted) and passes without corrective response or explicit expression -> unexpressed_divergence. Same reference item at a distinct point.
